resolved_suspects.description: Complex pointer cast (int-cast of parenthesized pointer arithmetic)

Pointer value `(pCVar7 + 4)` truncated by cast to `int` (sub-pointer width) — correct on the 32-bit matching build, a hard `cast from pointer to smaller type` error at 64-bit. If the value is used as an integer (delta, address print, hash), rewrite the cast as `uintptr_t`/`intptr_t` in a .keep.

Watcom field-by-field struct copy (3 consecutive `dst.field = src.field;` lines). Replace with `dst = src;` or `memcpy(&dst, &src, sizeof(...));` in a .keep — but only once the run (together with any sibling runs for the same dst/src pair) covers every byte of the struct. Collapsing a run that leaves a gap WIDENS the copy and changes behaviour; see `partial_struct_copy` (§31) for that case.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar7` self-updates via element-arithmetic `(int)(pCVar7 + N) + M`, where `N*sizeof(*pCVar7) + M` equals the larger struct stride being walked (the pointer is typed to a sub-element). Replace `pCVar7->field` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

stack_patterns.note: Function contains stack manipulation that may cause decompiler artifacts.

patterns.impact: Causes ESP-relative offsets to become runtime-dependent. All stack variables accessed via ESP after this point will appear as separate "in_stack_XXXX" parameters.
